This is great for Yonkers. All municipalities should have a dog park. However my experience with dog parks are not always safe. Most municipalities request registration of your pet. Although this seems excessive it ensures accountability for all dogs to be safe.  In New Rochelle the following applies for the Ward Acres Dog Park. 

Permit & Tags: Must have a visible permit and wear rabies/license tags.

Vaccinated (4+ Mos): Dogs must be 4+ months old and up-to-date on shots.

Spayed/Neutered: Dogs over 12 months must be fixed; no dogs in heat.

Handler Age: Supervisors must be at least 16 years old.

4-Dog Limit: Maximum of 3/4 dogs per handler inside the park.

These are rules that maybe the City of Yonkers should think about. 

Just my $.02

Permit & Tags: Must have a visible permit and wear rabies/license tags.

Vaccinated (4+ Mos): Dogs must be 4+ months old and up-to-date on shots.

Spayed/Neutered: Dogs over 12 months must be fixed; no dogs in heat.

Handler Age: Supervisors must be at least 16 years old.

4-Dog Limit: Maximum of 3/4 dogs per handler inside the park.

These are rules that maybe the City of Yonkers should think about.

In the 1980s, Yonkers stood on the brink of bankruptcy. Today, it stands as one of New York State’s major cities—a remarkable transformation that every resident should be proud of.

Yet pride alone cannot replace investment.

Too many neighborhoods. Too many housing developments. Too many schools. Too many community organizations. Too many opportunities remain underfunded while the same projects and the same select few continue to receive funding measured in the tens of millions of dollars.

As New York State prepares to implement its new Financial Literacy Requirement beginning this academic year, with Personal Finance at its core, the public deserves to know:

* What funding has been allocated?
* What resources are being provided?
* Who will deliver the instruction?
* How will every student benefit?

Financial literacy is not a luxury. It is an economic necessity.

We all appreciate beautification projects, but a serious question deserves a serious answer:

Will Financial Literacy receive the same level of attention, investment, urgency, and commitment as bricks, buildings, and beautification?

The future of Yonkers will not be determined solely by what we build around our children—but by what we build within them.

Yonkers is capable of leading New York State in preparing the next generation for financial independence, economic opportunity, and civic responsibility.

Because Yonkers is better than this.

We’re constantly told that overdevelopment will make our neighborhoods safer. But where is the evidence?

What many residents are actually seeing is more reckless driving, cars with modified exhausts, music so loud it shakes our walls, more public disturbances, and more visible drug activity. The problems haven’t disappeared, they’ve simply moved. As Pretty Woman said, “It’s geography.”

Meanwhile, the quality of life keeps slipping away. The Sawmill River is polluted. I reported a scooter bike and other debris in the water to the Parks Department two weeks before the Fourth of July, and as of this weekend, it was still there.

Residents keep reporting potholes, traffic problems, excessive honking, and noise. At the corner of Main Street and Riverdale Avenue, people constantly honk because there isn’t a clearly posted “Right Turn on Red” sign. It’s a simple issue that could easily be addressed.

Instead of focusing on basic quality of life, all we see is more overdevelopment and the destruction of what made Yonkers unique. Historic buildings, mature trees, murals, and green spaces disappear while new construction goes up.

And where is the accountability? At 87 Nepperhan Avenue, demolition took place without any visible dust mitigation despite concerns about dust and possible hazardous materials. Ironically, the Mayor’s own videos documented the conditions.

Residents deserve clean streets, clean parks, safer roads, responsible development, and a city government that addresses everyday problems, not just approves more buildings.
